semantic_fragments.content: Potential HAZARDOUS SITUATIONS, including that stem from or are triggered by USE ERRORS has been thoroughly analyzed. The probability of a HAZARDOUS SITUATION occurring and the likelihood of harm resulting from it are considered. We searched MAUDE of FDA with Infrared Forehead Thermometer, and found there are a few adverse events happen on Infrared Forehead Thermometer, in most cases, there is an error in the measurement of the infrared forehead thermometer. However, most of the event did not have complications from this incident, and the patient is doing well now.

5.1 Identify and describe hazard-related use scenarios evaluated
a) Normal USE SCENARIOS:
– OPERATOR/PATIENT = adult
– room temperature
– Adequate illumination
– Measure the body temperature when the environment is quiet

b) worst case USE SCENARIOS: PATIENT = OPERATOR:
– OPERATOR/PATIENT = adult
– Environmental temperature is 40°C, 95%RH
– unadequate illumination
– Measure body temperature when the environment is unquiet

The process of identifying known or foreseeable HAZARDS and HAZARDOUS SITUATIONS in the context of the Infrared Forehead Thermometer project involves various steps and considerations. This activity is an integral part of the RISK MANAGEMENT PROCESS, as outlined in ISO 14971, and is closely linked to the USABILITY ENGINEERING PROCESS. HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIOS has been defined as when a USE SCENARIO of Infrared Forehead Thermometer leads to a potentially dangerous situation for operators. Preliminary HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIOS that encompass various stages of USER interaction with the Infrared Forehead Thermometer has been identified in section 4 of the risk assessment report, demonstrated as Hazardous situation. These scenarios include details about the sequence of events, conditions, environments, and descriptions of the user interface.

5.2 Select hazard-related use scenarios for summative evaluation: The purpose of selecting Hazard-Related Use Scenarios for summative evaluation in the context of a Infrared Forehead Thermometer is to ensure that the evaluation process covers all potential safety-related aspects of the device's user interface. Given that a Infrared Forehead Thermometer is considered a simple device, and as a mature device, its use is not likely to result in severe harm, so all potential scenarios will be included in the summative evaluation, regardless of the severity of potential harm. This option would provide a comprehensive assessment of the device's user interface under various usage conditions and would likely cover a wide range of potential use errors.

5.3 Establish user interface specification: The user interface specification for the Infrared Forehead Thermometer is as follows:
a. Visual Design and Layout: The device and the display should be easily readable, button should be easily understandable, user can complete the measurement with only the device and instruction for use.
b. Feedback and Indicators: Provide clear visual feedback to confirm device operation, mode, and settings. Indicate battery status.
c. Safety Features: Incorporate features to prevent accidental changes in settings during use. Implement user lock-out mechanisms to avoid unintended modifications.
d. Usability Testing: Conduct usability testing with representative users according to EN 62366-1 standard to validate the effectiveness and ease of use. Identify potential use errors and areas for improvement based on user feedback.

6. Perform user interface design:
(1) General: The user interface design input is conducted prioritizing meeting established user interface requirements from users. The design process is iterative and aims to develop a user interface that permits users to perform all hazard-based use scenarios acceptably.
(2) Develop Conceptual Model(s): Create a conceptual model that describes the general organization of the user interface, refer to the previous generation device, which has been in the EU market.
(3) Design Software and Hardware User Interfaces: The software function of the device is simple, the software user interface is only indication on LCD, this indication should easy to be understood. The hardware user interface includes main device, probe and wires. Develop concept sketches to explore various hardware design concepts and obtain user feedback.
(4) Develop Detailed Designs: Develop integrated software and hardware user interface designs based on refined concepts. Use iterative development and formative evaluations to refine and improve designs. Create user interface designs that reflect both software and hardware components, ensuring proper integration.
